messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] scantwo (Haley Knott). Error in subset.cross
parts:
Is the error occurring at fatScan or at fatPerm?

What makes you say that it's a bug?
Please show the results of the following:

nphe(f2g)
sum(!is.na(f2g$pheno[,8])
sum(!is.na(sex))
sum(!is.na(f2g$pheno[,8]) & !is.na(sex))

I would upgrade R to 2.15.1; 2.11.1 is two years old.

karl



On Jun 28, 2012, at 1:10 PM, Justin Hendrick wrote:

> R version: 2.11.1
> R/QTL version: 1.24-9
>
> Here is the code that produces the error:
>
> f2g = calc.genoprob(f2g, step=20, stepwidth="fixed", map.function="c-f", err=0.002)
> fatScan = scantwo(f2g, pheno.col=c(8), addcovar=sex, method="hk")
> fatPerm = scantwo(f2g, pheno.col=c(8), addcovar=sex, method="hk", n.perm=10, verbose=FALSE)
>
> and here is the error:
>
> Error in subset.cross(cross, ind = keep.ind.boolean) :
> Must retain at least one individual.
> Calls: scantwo -> checkcovar -> subset.cross
> Execution halted
>
> This looks like the same bug that was in 1.22-21. (My MouseID column is numeric).
>

messages.author: 06c9fbe0cdfa0652
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] scantwo (Haley Knott). Error in subset.cross
parts:
fatScan

I think it might be a bug because it sounds a lot like this (from www.rqtl.org/BUGS.txt):

"2. Bug in checkcovar (in util.R) regarding omitting individuals with
      missing phenotypes when there's an ID column with numeric values.
      The wrong individuals get omitted from the cross. [Fixed in
      Version 1.24-9.]"

> nphe(f2g)
[1] 16
> sum(!is.na(f2g$pheno[,8]))
[1] 842
> sum(!is.na(sex))
[1] 2054
> sum(!is.na(f2g$pheno[,8]) & !is.na(sex))

[1] 842

I am working on a cluster so I have limited control over software versions (but I'll see if I can update it).

Thanks for the response
Justin
